fact: Governor Saamoi says the Central Bank of Liberia launched the Inclusive Instant Payment System (Pay Na-Na), mobile money interoperability, as the first phase of the National Electronic Payment Switch, with a pilot completed earlier in 2025.
CBL Directive 002/2025 applies to all licensed Mobile Money Providers and threatens sanctions up to licence revocation under the New Payment Systems Law 2014 and Mobile Money Regulations 2014.

The Central Bank of Liberia directs that Government of Liberia mobile money payments and revenue collections be routed exclusively through NEPS/IIPS, with settlement at the CBL and monitoring of implementation by the CBL.
The Central Bank of Liberia launched the Inclusive Instant Payment System in December 2025, connecting the Lonestar MTN and Orange Liberia mobile-money platforms, per the outlet and the bank.

The Central Bank of Liberia deputy governor says the CBL's reforms include the RTGS, the ACH and a recently launched instant and interoperable payment system operating across banks and mobile network operators.
A Central Bank of Liberia speaker says the central bank built the country's instant payment system, launched in 73 days, with banks and mobile money operators integrated.
The Central Bank of Liberia approved a unified fee regime for interoperable P2P transfers on the Inclusive Instant Payments System (Pay Na-Na), launched 16 December 2025.

FrontPage Africa says the Central Bank of Liberia spearheaded the launch of the Inclusive Instant Payment System, a nationwide mobile money interoperability platform, with the World Bank supporting a full National Electronic Payment Switch.
The Central Bank of Liberia's Executive Governor said PAPSS was officially launched in Liberia on 27 March 2025, with the central bank as settlement agent.
